title: Relatives and George Lewis gigs
summary: Miele Barnes, Lawrence Marrero and others are family; he played neighborhood gigs with George Lewis.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: Oh, you didn't tell me much about Miele Barnes.

Well, Miele, I knew Miele all my life. Miele related to me. But I never played with him or, you know, and the only time I really got to really him, Miele, been a nice fellow all the days, but the only time I got to him was, you know, when he's the preservation, all opened up and all that, you know. But like Miele, Paul Barnes, all that's my relatives, Saif Frazier, Lawrence Marrero, all that's family. Very close too. Sisters and brothers, children, you know.
But what about George Lutz? Did you have an album here?
Oh, George, sure. I know George. He's a good friend of George all my young life. I played gigs with George. I know George. Yes, indeed.
Where did you play the gigs with George?

I played gigs all around New Orleans with George. George played the Caldone. He played gigs. He played gigs. Like I was telling you, down around Franklin Avenue and Charters, all around there, before he'd come before they played, Boehme Street. All around Decatur Street, Charter Street. Manavill and Charters. All around St. Rock Street. Those neighborhoods, you'd have many neighborhoods, many neighborhoods, ballrooms during them times that had music. Yeah. You know? Neighborhood ballroom that had music. Yeah. And then you got so now, you got to get a job on Boehme Street, but you used to go play at the corner of your house, man. You know what I'm talking about? And a giant or something like that, too. An old giant one's talking about.
